intro: Orroroo is a small town in South Australia's northern Flinders Ranges, a long drive north of Adelaide. At its edge stands the Giant Gum, a river red gum that the District Council of Orroroo/Carrieton's own sign puts at more than 500 years old and 10.89 metres round. Other measurements, from an older sign and a national register of big trees, come out a little smaller, so the page gives the spread. It stands on public ground beside its sign and costs nothing to visit.

trees.name: The Orroroo Giant Gum
trees.age_estimate: more than 500 years, by the council's sign
trees.story:
On the edge of Orroroo, a small town in South Australia's northern Flinders Ranges, a river red gum stands with a trunk wide enough that a man with outstretched arms covers a fraction of it. A sign beside it, put up by the District Council of Orroroo/Carrieton, gives its circumference as 10.89 metres at 0.61 metres above the ground and its age as estimated in excess of 500 years.

Other figures disagree a little. An older sign gave about 10.4 metres, and the National Register of Big Trees records a measurement of 9.90 metres at breast height in 2009 with an age of 485 years. The differences come from where and when the tape went round, and the age is an estimate in every source, so read it as roughly five centuries.

Visitors know it simply as the Giant Gum. Pale, peeling limbs fork from the top of a deeply furrowed trunk, and the bark near the base is rough and dark.

It stands on public ground by the roadside with the sign in front, so no ticket or permission is needed.
